new.n: Mainland opposite La Pointe: 800 lb copper boulder (1845)
new.st: Col. Charles Whittlesey recorded a copper boulder of about 800 pounds found in 1845 on the mainland opposite La Pointe (Madeline Island). R. D. Salisbury repeated the record in his 1883 compilation of drift copper finds. No closer spot is given; the pin is Bayfield, the mainland town that faces La Pointe.
new.t: Red clay bluffs and stream cuts along the Bayfield shore. Work gravel bars below eroding clay banks, and the beach after a northeast blow. Private and tribal land is close by: ask first.
src: Salisbury, Notes on the Dispersion of Drift Copper, Trans. Wisconsin Academy vol. VI (1881-83), p. 46, quoting Whittlesey (Smithsonian Contributions, 1866)

new.pl: Mainland shore opposite La Pointe; the pin is Bayfield

new.n: Middle fork of the Ontonagon: 300-400 lb boulder in red clay
new.st: Whittlesey, quoted by Salisbury (1883): 'Three miles south of the Minnesota Mine on middle fork of the Ontonagon, another copper bowlder was taken from the red clay, which weighed between three and four hundred pounds.' The pin is three miles due south of the Minesota Mine at Rockland; the record names no closer spot.
new.t: River cutbanks in red clay and the gravel bars just below them. Most of this ground is private or Commercial Forest land, which is open to the public for hunting, fishing and trapping only, not digging: ask the owner.

new.st: Whittlesey recorded a chunk of copper of three or four pounds at the mouth of the Menominee River (Salisbury 1883). The pin is the river mouth between Marinette and Menominee.
new.t: Beach and river-mouth gravels after storms and low water. Town shoreline and harbor: check local rules before digging.

new.v: About 30 pieces on record; one over 7 lb at Geneva Lake; a 40-50 lb boulder near the state line
new.st: Chamberlin had record of about thirty pieces of drift copper from Walworth County, and one found at Geneva Lake weighed upward of seven pounds. Whittlesey noted a boulder of forty or fifty pounds in Walworth County near the state line (Salisbury 1883). Chamberlin also wrote that copper is frequently found at all points along the Kettle Moraine, which crosses the county. The pin is the city of Lake Geneva; no single find is placed closer.
new.t: Plowed fields after spring rain and the gravel pits of the Kettle Moraine, with permission. Kettle Moraine State Forest land: look only.

new.v: Two pieces of float copper picked up on the beach
new.st: R. D. Salisbury picked up two pieces of copper on the Lake Michigan shore in Ozaukee County after a severe storm. He thought they had washed out of the red clay that borders the lake there; both were irregular, not water-worn (Salisbury 1883). Only the county shore is given; the pin is Port Washington.
new.t: Walk the beach below the clay bluffs after a big northeast blow, when fresh clay has slumped and the waves have sorted it. The bluffs slump without warning: stay off the toe after rain. Check each beach's own rules.

new.st: Salisbury (1883), from the Minnesota survey reports, lists copper found at Pleasant Grove in Olmsted County, and in Fillmore County with no place given. This is old drift at the western edge of the Driftless Area, so finds are rare. The pin is Pleasant Grove Township.
new.t: Old, deeply weathered drift: plowed fields and stream gravels with permission. Expect single small pieces.

new.v: A copper mass that sold for $80
new.st: A mass of copper found at Northport, Leelanau County, sold for $80, which Salisbury (1883) took to mean it was of great size. He also noted copper 'frequently met with' in Benzie, Antrim and Grand Traverse counties, and named Grand Traverse Bay as one of the places drift copper seemed most plentiful. The pin is the village.
new.t: Fields, gravel pits and the bay shore after storms, with permission.

new.n: Ada copper the size of a fist (Kent Co.)
new.v: Fist-size piece, with frequent smaller fragments
new.st: Whittlesey described a piece of copper the size of a man's fist from Ada, Kent County, with frequent smaller fragments (Salisbury 1883). The pin is Ada Township.
new.t: Grand River valley gravels and fields with permission.
